claimed_class: F115 Security controls bypass or absence (header-trusted client IP, per worklist reference getClientIpAddress)
reason: Target and control/role tests fail: getRealIp already prefers X-Real-IP then X-Forwarded-For over the TCP peer address, so on the clean baseline it is already the reference's header-trust shape — there is no control here to weaken — and its only clean-baseline consumer is the audit log (RequestAudit), not a security decision. The genuine F115 realization of this header-trust is SCGD-002, which wires getRealIp into the rate-limit KeyResolver as the tainted source.

claimed_class: F115 Security controls bypass or absence (mTLS/SPIFFE intra-namespace auth backdoor, per worklist reference)
reason: Class-match and target tests fail: the reference is an authentication filter that returns MISSING_HEADERS/UNAUTHORIZED and gates the chain, so its isIntraNamespaceRequest(mtlsHeader) early-return is a real auth bypass. AuditFilter.filter makes no auth decision — it always forwards via chain.filter and only writes an audit document to Mongo (its one branch is the audit.enabled property). Porting the mtls early-return here would guard nothing; at most it suppresses the audit record, which the genuineness gate treats as a logging (non-control) forced signal. Authentication in this app lives in SecurityConfiguration (OIDC) and IpFilter, not here.

Control/role and class-match tests fail: createAuditLog fills a DTO for logging and already takes the IP from the header-trusting IpUtils.getRealIp; replacing it with another header changes a log field, not a rate-limit key or any enforcement. The resulting defect would be log spoofing / traceability, not F115. (Not in the current worklist; retained from the prior candidate hand-off.)
